That's not how Federal income taxes work. You pay the percentage in each bracket before moving to the next. For example, if you are single and have an even $100,000 in taxable income in 2020, you pay:

  • 0% on income between $0 and $12,400 = $0
  • 10% on income between $12,400 and $22,275 = $987.50
  • 12% on income between $22,275 and $52,525 = $3,630
  • 22% on income between $52,525 and $97,925 = $9,988
  • 24% on income between $97,925 and $100,000 = $498

Total Federal income tax = $15,103.50, not 24% of $100,000.

A single person only needs to have about $131,000 in taxable income to be paying $1,200 every two weeks in Federal income tax.
